pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

- Converts destinationCalendar on CalendarEvent to be an array.
- Patches and fixes so every sentence of code that was using evet.destinationCalendar can support the new type of array.
- The logic here is to fallback to normal behaviour has having one main destinationCalendar but also supports multiple so host can get invited correctly.

Fixes #7754 
## Loom 
Creating event and rescheduling:
https://www.loom.com/share/3cb3af513d274ed2bdfed44e48edddf6?sid=d81ce3de-2893-4a30-b085-ff67c31b7dfb

Canceling event:
https://www.loom.com/share/7ef505d4665e4d4982d2bb2d7b118085?sid=cd43c97c-aa86-4667-979f-f6492adf3365

## Requirement/Documentation

## Type of change

<!-- Please delete bullets that are not relevant. -->

- [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How should this be tested?

- Are there environment variables that should be set? No
- What are the minimal test data to have? Setup a collective event using teampro and teamfree users. Add any app calendar to those accounts and add them as host for collective event.
- What is expected (happy path) to have (input and output)? Collective event with 2 host and every user with any calendar app installed should receive proper calendar events.
- Any other important info that could help to test that PR

## Mandatory Tasks

- [X] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to a destination calendar matched by the service's credential (or the first destination calendar) instead of comparing externalId against the known-falsy externalCalendarId.
raw_findings.title: Tautological find() in Google deleteEvent silently redirects deletes to the 'primary' calendar
raw_findings.trigger: deleteEvent is called with a null/undefined externalCalendarId for a booking whose event was created on a non-primary destination calendar; the fallback branch compares against the falsy externalCalendarId and never matches.

raw_findings.body: The recreated booking references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId (previously sourced from `evt.destinationCalendar`), so subsequent updates/cancellations cannot resolve the right calendar or credential and fall into wrong-calendar/'primary' fallbacks.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Booking references are silently rewritten with undefined calendar/credential linkage after a location edit.
raw_findings.impact: The recreated booking references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId (previously sourced from `evt.destinationCalendar`), so subsequent updates/cancellations cannot resolve the right calendar or credential and fall into wrong-calendar/'primary' fallbacks.
raw_findings.root_cause: The refactor assumes every EventResult carries externalId/credentialId, but only the create path was updated to populate them; the update path still returns results without these fields.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Have CalendarManager.updateEvent include `credentialId: credential.id` and the resolved externalCalendarId in its returned EventResult, or preserve these fields from the existing reference when rebuilding referencesToCreate.
raw_findings.title: updateLocation references read externalId/credentialId from updateEvent results that never set them
raw_findings.trigger: A booking location is edited (updateLocation), which rebuilds referencesToCreate from updateEvent results; CalendarManager.updateEvent's returned EventResult contains neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`.

raw_findings.body: The EventResult's `externalId` is undefined, so EventManager.create now writes `externalCalendarId: undefined` into the booking reference (previously populated from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), degrading later update/delete calls into wrong-calendar fallbacks.
raw_findings.failure_mode: References for legacy destination calendars are persisted without externalCalendarId.
raw_findings.impact: The EventResult's `externalId` is undefined, so EventManager.create now writes `externalCalendarId: undefined` into the booking reference (previously populated from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), degrading later update/delete calls into wrong-calendar fallbacks.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only the credentialId branch of the loop was updated to forward the destination externalId to createEvent.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument in this branch too: `createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId)`.
raw_findings.title: createEvent called without externalId in the no-credentialId destination branch, losing externalCalendarId on references
raw_findings.trigger: A booking targets a legacy destination calendar record without a credentialId; createAllCalendarEvents takes the else-branch and calls createEvent without the new third `externalId` argument.

raw_findings.body: The service posts to `/me/calendars/{organizer's externalId}/events` using the host's token; the externalId does not exist in the host's account, so the Graph API returns 404 and the host never gets the event on their calendar, defeating the PR's multi-host goal. The same first-element pattern is repeated in the Lark service.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Calendar event creation fails or lands on the wrong calendar for secondary hosts on non-Google providers.
raw_findings.impact: The service posts to `/me/calendars/{organizer's externalId}/events` using the host's token; the externalId does not exist in the host's account, so the Graph API returns 404 and the host never gets the event on their calendar, defeating the PR's multi-host goal. The same first-element pattern is repeated in the Lark service.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only GoogleCalendarService was updated to match the destination calendar by credentialId; other services blindly take the first array element.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Select the destination calendar matching the invoking credential (accept the credentialId parameter like the Google service and use `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), falling back to `/me/calendar/events` when no match exists.
raw_findings.title: Office365 createEvent targets the first destination calendar regardless of which host's credential is in use
raw_findings.trigger: A collective team booking where a non-organizer host uses Office 365: createAllCalendarEvents invokes this service with the host's credential, but destinationCalendar[0] is the organizer's/event-type's calendar (possibly from a different provider or account).

raw_findings.body: `?.push` on null is a no-op, so all collected teamDestinationCalendars are discarded; secondary hosts do not receive calendar events, which is the exact scenario this PR intends to fix.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Host destination calendars collected for collective events never reach EventManager.
raw_findings.impact: `?.push` on null is a no-op, so all collected teamDestinationCalendars are discarded; secondary hosts do not receive calendar events, which is the exact scenario this PR intends to fix.
raw_findings.root_cause: Optional chaining on a nullable array combined with a `null` fallback initializer makes the push silently skip.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize destinationCalendar to `[]` instead of `null` in the evt construction (or assign `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`).
raw_findings.title: Team hosts' destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has none
raw_findings.trigger: A collective team booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `null` at R1067) but other hosts do have destination calendars.

raw_findings.body: Downstream code that previously relied on `user.organization.slug` for dynamic bookings (e.g., org-scoped booker URLs/usernames) receives undefined, producing incorrect links or behavior for organization users.

raw_findings.impact: Downstream code that previously relied on `user.organization.slug` for dynamic bookings (e.g., org-scoped booker URLs/usernames) receives undefined, producing incorrect links or behavior for organization users.
raw_findings.root_cause: The rewrite of loadUsers omitted the previously selected organization relation from the findMany select clause.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Re-add `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` to the prisma select in the !eventTypeId branch, or verify and document that no consumer reads user.organization after loadUsers.

raw_findings.trigger: A dynamic group booking (no eventTypeId) is created for users belonging to an organization; loadUsers now selects only userSelect fields, credentials, and metadata.

raw_findings.body: The same calendar events are deleted N times (once per reference); subsequent attempts hit already-deleted events, generating avoidable API errors/rejections in the awaited Promise.all and log noise.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate delete requests against calendar APIs during recurring cancellation.
raw_findings.impact: The same calendar events are deleted N times (once per reference); subsequent attempts hit already-deleted events, generating avoidable API errors/rejections in the awaited Promise.all and log noise.
raw_findings.root_cause: Wrapping the existing single-reference logic in a loop without excluding the branch that already iterates over all credentials and bookings.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Hoist the recurring-event bulk-deletion branch out of the per-reference loop (run it once), keeping only the single-event `deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` path per reference.
raw_findings.title: Recurring-event deletion block now runs once per calendar reference, issuing duplicate deletes
raw_findings.trigger: Cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring team event whose booking has two or more calendar references with credentialIds: the recurring branch inside the new per-reference loop iterates all user calendar credentials and all updated bookings for every reference.

raw_findings.body: TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`) is thrown at EventManager.create, aborting booking creation entirely for users who select Google Meet without a destination calendar, instead of the intended fallback to Cal Video.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled runtime TypeError during booking creation breaks the Google Meet -> Cal Video fallback path for any host lacking a destination calendar.
raw_findings.impact: TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`) is thrown at EventManager.create, aborting booking creation entirely for users who select Google Meet without a destination calendar, instead of the intended fallback to Cal Video.
raw_findings.root_cause: Changing CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar from a single nullable object to a nullable array introduced array destructuring at consumer sites; the destructured element can be undefined for empty/null arrays, but TypeScript types it as DestinationCalendar, so the missing optional chain in EventManager.create's Meet fallback check was not caught.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the destructured value: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` (or an explicit length/null check) in EventManager.create before accessing `.integration`; alternatively type the destructured element as possibly undefined and handle it.
raw_findings.title: Array conversion of destinationCalendar leaves unguarded dereference crashing Google Meet fallback
raw_findings.trigger: A booking is created with location set to Google Meet (MeetLocationType) while evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (e.g., organizer has no destination calendar configured); EventManager.create destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without a guard.

raw_findings.body: For collective events whose organizer lacks a destination calendar, the other hosts' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are never added to the event, so those hosts do not receive calendar events — defeating the PR's stated purpose of inviting all collective hosts correctly.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent data loss: valid team host destination calendars are discarded without any error, producing bookings that skip some hosts' calendars.
raw_findings.impact: For collective events whose organizer lacks a destination calendar, the other hosts' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are never added to the event, so those hosts do not receive calendar events — defeating the PR's stated purpose of inviting all collective hosts correctly.
raw_findings.root_cause: The array-typed field allows a null base value, and the aggregation code appends team calendars with optional chaining, silently skipping the append when the base is null instead of creating the array.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize evt.destinationCalendar to an empty array (or `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`) so team destination calendars are always appended regardless of the organizer's configuration.
raw_findings.title: Team hosts' destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
raw_findings.trigger: A COLLECTIVE team booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar: handleNewBooking initializes `destinationCalendar: ... : null`, so the later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` optional-chains into a no-op even when other team hosts do have destination calendars.

raw_findings.body: The mandatory second parameter is a breaking change to the widely implemented Calendar contract: single-argument call sites fail type-checking, and 12 implementations silently ignore a value the interface now claims is required, misleading future implementers.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Compile-time breakage for external/one-argument callers and a misleading contract where most implementations do not honor the required parameter.
raw_findings.impact: The mandatory second parameter is a breaking change to the widely implemented Calendar contract: single-argument call sites fail type-checking, and 12 implementations silently ignore a value the interface now claims is required, misleading future implementers.
raw_findings.root_cause: The interface was tightened to a required parameter to serve a single implementation's need instead of using an optional parameter.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Declare the parameter as optional (`credentialId?: number`) in the Calendar interface, since CalendarManager always supplies it and only GoogleCalendarService needs it, preserving compatibility for existing single-argument callers.
raw_findings.title: Calendar.createEvent gains a required credentialId parameter used by only one implementation
raw_findings.trigger: Any caller of the shared Calendar interface (tests, API handlers, third-party app-store integrations, or future code) that invokes `calendar.createEvent(event)` with a single argument; among the 13 in-repo CalendarService implementations, only googlecalendar consumes the new parameter.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the null/empty-array handling paths (e.g., the Meet fallback crash and silent team-calendar drop) can ship undetected, and future refactors of destinationCalendar consumers have no safety net.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Review and CI cannot detect breakage in the many consumer sites rewritten for the array type, leaving the collective multi-host behavior unverified.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the null/empty-array handling paths (e.g., the Meet fallback crash and silent team-calendar drop) can ship undetected, and future refactors of destinationCalendar consumers have no safety net.
raw_findings.root_cause: A cross-cutting data-shape change to a core type was merged without any accompanying test coverage of the new array semantics.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add unit/integration tests exercising EventManager.create and handleNewBooking with destinationCalendar as null, empty array, single-element, and multi-host arrays (collective event with two hosts), asserting each host's calendar receives the event and no crash occurs when it is absent.
raw_findings.title: No tests cover the destinationCalendar single-object-to-array conversion
raw_findings.trigger: The PR converts destinationCalendar to an array and touches booking creation, reschedule, and cancel flows across EventManager and multiple calendar services (google, lark, office365), yet the PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added; edge cases like empty array, null, and multi-host arrays are untested.

finding.failure_mode: Cancelled bookings leave orphaned events on the actual Google calendar.
finding.impact: calendarId resolves to undefined and the subsequent `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` sends the delete to 'primary', where the event does not exist; the original calendar event is left undeleted on cancellation (previously the destination calendar externalId was used).
finding.root_cause: Copy of the same faulty fallback predicate used in updateEvent: matching on the falsy parameter instead of a meaningful key.
finding.suggested_fix: Fall back to a destination calendar matched by the service's credential (or the first destination calendar) instead of comparing externalId against the known-falsy externalCalendarId.
finding.title: Tautological find() in Google deleteEvent silently redirects deletes to the 'primary' calendar
finding.trigger: deleteEvent is called with a null/undefined externalCalendarId for a booking whose event was created on a non-primary destination calendar; the fallback branch compares against the falsy externalCalendarId and never matches.
finding.verifier_reason: Same tautological find pattern at R315-317 in deleteEvent as candidate 3's updateEvent. Same root cause, same fix needed. Merging into candidate 3.

finding.body: The recreated booking references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId (previously sourced from `evt.destinationCalendar`), so subsequent updates/cancellations cannot resolve the right calendar or credential and fall into wrong-calendar/'primary' fallbacks.
finding.failure_mode: Booking references are silently rewritten with undefined calendar/credential linkage after a location edit.
finding.impact: The recreated booking references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId (previously sourced from `evt.destinationCalendar`), so subsequent updates/cancellations cannot resolve the right calendar or credential and fall into wrong-calendar/'primary' fallbacks.
finding.root_cause: The refactor assumes every EventResult carries externalId/credentialId, but only the create path was updated to populate them; the update path still returns results without these fields.
finding.suggested_fix: Have CalendarManager.updateEvent include `credentialId: credential.id` and the resolved externalCalendarId in its returned EventResult, or preserve these fields from the existing reference when rebuilding referencesToCreate.
finding.title: updateLocation references read externalId/credentialId from updateEvent results that never set them
finding.trigger: A booking location is edited (updateLocation), which rebuilds referencesToCreate from updateEvent results; CalendarManager.updateEvent's returned EventResult contains neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`.
finding.verifier_reason: Patch R208-209 shows updateLocation reads `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId` from updateEvent results. CalendarManager.updateEvent (L313-322) returns EventResult without externalId or credentialId fields, so these will be undefined.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.850 is below 0.920: Patch R208-209 shows updateLocation reads `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId` from updateEvent results. finding.failure_mode: References for legacy destination calendars are persisted without externalCalendarId.
finding.impact: The EventResult's `externalId` is undefined, so EventManager.create now writes `externalCalendarId: undefined` into the booking reference (previously populated from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), degrading later update/delete calls into wrong-calendar fallbacks.
finding.root_cause: Only the credentialId branch of the loop was updated to forward the destination externalId to createEvent.
finding.suggested_fix: Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument in this branch too: `createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId)`.
finding.title: createEvent called without externalId in the no-credentialId destination branch, losing externalCalendarId on references
finding.trigger: A booking targets a legacy destination calendar record without a credentialId; createAllCalendarEvents takes the else-branch and calls createEvent without the new third `externalId` argument.
finding.verifier_reason: Patch R380 shows `createEvent(c, event)` called without third externalId argument in the else branch (no credentialId). The if branch at R370 passes `destination.externalId`, but else branch omits it, losing externalCalendarId on references.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.800 is below 0.920: Patch R380 shows `createEvent(c, event)` called without third externalId argument in the else branch (no credentialId). The if branch at R370 passes `destination.externalId`, but else branch omits it, losing externalCalendarId on references.

finding.body: The service posts to `/me/calendars/{organizer's externalId}/events` using the host's token; the externalId does not exist in the host's account, so the Graph API returns 404 and the host never gets the event on their calendar, defeating the PR's multi-host goal. The same first-element pattern is repeated in the Lark service.
finding.failure_mode: Calendar event creation fails or lands on the wrong calendar for secondary hosts on non-Google providers.
finding.impact: The service posts to `/me/calendars/{organizer's externalId}/events` using the host's token; the externalId does not exist in the host's account, so the Graph API returns 404 and the host never gets the event on their calendar, defeating the PR's multi-host goal. The same first-element pattern is repeated in the Lark service.
finding.root_cause: Only GoogleCalendarService was updated to match the destination calendar by credentialId; other services blindly take the first array element.
finding.suggested_fix: Select the destination calendar matching the invoking credential (accept the credentialId parameter like the Google service and use `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), falling back to `/me/calendar/events` when no match exists.
finding.title: Office365 createEvent targets the first destination calendar regardless of which host's credential is in use
finding.trigger: A collective team booking where a non-organizer host uses Office 365: createAllCalendarEvents invokes this service with the host's credential, but destinationCalendar[0] is the organizer's/event-type's calendar (possibly from a different provider or account).
finding.verifier_reason: Patch R73 shows Office365 destructures first element of destinationCalendar array. For collective team bookings with multiple hosts, each host's credential invokes this service but uses organizer's calendar externalId, which may not exist in the host's account.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.700 is below 0.920: Patch R73 shows Office365 destructures first element of destinationCalendar array. For collective team bookings with multiple hosts, each host's credential invokes this service but uses organizer's calendar externalId, which may not exist in the host's account.

finding.body: `?.push` on null is a no-op, so all collected teamDestinationCalendars are discarded; secondary hosts do not receive calendar events, which is the exact scenario this PR intends to fix.
finding.failure_mode: Host destination calendars collected for collective events never reach EventManager.
finding.impact: `?.push` on null is a no-op, so all collected teamDestinationCalendars are discarded; secondary hosts do not receive calendar events, which is the exact scenario this PR intends to fix.
finding.root_cause: Optional chaining on a nullable array combined with a `null` fallback initializer makes the push silently skip.
finding.suggested_fix: Initialize destinationCalendar to `[]` instead of `null` in the evt construction (or assign `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`).
finding.title: Team hosts' destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has none
finding.trigger: A collective team booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `null` at R1067) but other hosts do have destination calendars.
finding.verifier_reason: Patch R1077-1079 shows `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. When destinationCalendar is null (R1067), optional chaining makes push a no-op, silently discarding team calendars.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.850 is below 0.920: Patch R1077-1079 shows `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. When destinationCalendar is null (R1067), optional chaining makes push a no-op, silently discarding team calendars.

finding.body: The same calendar events are deleted N times (once per reference); subsequent attempts hit already-deleted events, generating avoidable API errors/rejections in the awaited Promise.all and log noise.
finding.failure_mode: Duplicate delete requests against calendar APIs during recurring cancellation.
finding.impact: The same calendar events are deleted N times (once per reference); subsequent attempts hit already-deleted events, generating avoidable API errors/rejections in the awaited Promise.all and log noise.
finding.root_cause: Wrapping the existing single-reference logic in a loop without excluding the branch that already iterates over all credentials and bookings.
finding.suggested_fix: Hoist the recurring-event bulk-deletion branch out of the per-reference loop (run it once), keeping only the single-event `deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` path per reference.
finding.title: Recurring-event deletion block now runs once per calendar reference, issuing duplicate deletes
finding.trigger: Cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring team event whose booking has two or more calendar references with credentialIds: the recurring branch inside the new per-reference loop iterates all user calendar credentials and all updated bookings for every reference.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch shows a refactor of cancellation logic. The candidate claims duplicate deletes, but the new loop iterates per-reference and the recurring branch is not shown in the provided patch context. Cannot verify the duplicate deletion claim from available evidence.

rejected_findings.reason: The patch shows a refactor of cancellation logic. The candidate claims duplicate deletes, but the new loop iterates per-reference and the recurring branch is not shown in the provided patch context. Cannot verify the duplicate deletion claim from available evidence.

finding.body: TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`) is thrown at EventManager.create, aborting booking creation entirely for users who select Google Meet without a destination calendar, instead of the intended fallback to Cal Video.
finding.failure_mode: Unhandled runtime TypeError during booking creation breaks the Google Meet -> Cal Video fallback path for any host lacking a destination calendar.
finding.impact: TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`) is thrown at EventManager.create, aborting booking creation entirely for users who select Google Meet without a destination calendar, instead of the intended fallback to Cal Video.
finding.root_cause: Changing CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar from a single nullable object to a nullable array introduced array destructuring at consumer sites; the destructured element can be undefined for empty/null arrays, but TypeScript types it as DestinationCalendar, so the missing optional chain in EventManager.create's Meet fallback check was not caught.
finding.suggested_fix: Guard the destructured value: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` (or an explicit length/null check) in EventManager.create before accessing `.integration`; alternatively type the destructured element as possibly undefined and handle it.
finding.title: Array conversion of destinationCalendar leaves unguarded dereference crashing Google Meet fallback
finding.trigger: A booking is created with location set to Google Meet (MeetLocationType) while evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (e.g., organizer has no destination calendar configured); EventManager.create destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without a guard.
finding.verifier_reason: Same issue as candidate 0: missing optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration causing TypeError. Same root cause, same fix location. Merging into candidate 0.

finding.body: For collective events whose organizer lacks a destination calendar, the other hosts' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are never added to the event, so those hosts do not receive calendar events — defeating the PR's stated purpose of inviting all collective hosts correctly.
finding.failure_mode: Silent data loss: valid team host destination calendars are discarded without any error, producing bookings that skip some hosts' calendars.
finding.impact: For collective events whose organizer lacks a destination calendar, the other hosts' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are never added to the event, so those hosts do not receive calendar events — defeating the PR's stated purpose of inviting all collective hosts correctly.
finding.root_cause: The array-typed field allows a null base value, and the aggregation code appends team calendars with optional chaining, silently skipping the append when the base is null instead of creating the array.
finding.suggested_fix: Initialize evt.destinationCalendar to an empty array (or `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`) so team destination calendars are always appended regardless of the organizer's configuration.
finding.title: Team hosts' destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
finding.trigger: A COLLECTIVE team booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar: handleNewBooking initializes `destinationCalendar: ... : null`, so the later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` optional-chains into a no-op even when other team hosts do have destination calendars.
finding.verifier_reason: Same issue as candidate 8: team calendars dropped when destinationCalendar is null due to optional chaining on push. Same root cause and fix. Merging into candidate 8.

finding.body: The mandatory second parameter is a breaking change to the widely implemented Calendar contract: single-argument call sites fail type-checking, and 12 implementations silently ignore a value the interface now claims is required, misleading future implementers.
finding.failure_mode: Compile-time breakage for external/one-argument callers and a misleading contract where most implementations do not honor the required parameter.
finding.impact: The mandatory second parameter is a breaking change to the widely implemented Calendar contract: single-argument call sites fail type-checking, and 12 implementations silently ignore a value the interface now claims is required, misleading future implementers.
finding.root_cause: The interface was tightened to a required parameter to serve a single implementation's need instead of using an optional parameter.
finding.suggested_fix: Declare the parameter as optional (`credentialId?: number`) in the Calendar interface, since CalendarManager always supplies it and only GoogleCalendarService needs it, preserving compatibility for existing single-argument callers.
finding.title: Calendar.createEvent gains a required credentialId parameter used by only one implementation
finding.trigger: Any caller of the shared Calendar interface (tests, API handlers, third-party app-store integrations, or future code) that invokes `calendar.createEvent(event)` with a single argument; among the 13 in-repo CalendarService implementations, only googlecalendar consumes the new parameter.
finding.verifier_reason: The interface change to require credentialId is intentional design. CalendarManager.createEvent always passes credential.id (L236). The 12 implementations not using it is existing behavior, not a regression. This is a design/style concern, not a bug.

rejected_findings.reason: The interface change to require credentialId is intentional design. CalendarManager.createEvent always passes credential.id (L236). The 12 implementations not using it is existing behavior, not a regression. This is a design/style concern, not a bug.

finding.body: Regressions in the null/empty-array handling paths (e.g., the Meet fallback crash and silent team-calendar drop) can ship undetected, and future refactors of destinationCalendar consumers have no safety net.
finding.failure_mode: Review and CI cannot detect breakage in the many consumer sites rewritten for the array type, leaving the collective multi-host behavior unverified.
finding.impact: Regressions in the null/empty-array handling paths (e.g., the Meet fallback crash and silent team-calendar drop) can ship undetected, and future refactors of destinationCalendar consumers have no safety net.
finding.root_cause: A cross-cutting data-shape change to a core type was merged without any accompanying test coverage of the new array semantics.
finding.suggested_fix: Add unit/integration tests exercising EventManager.create and handleNewBooking with destinationCalendar as null, empty array, single-element, and multi-host arrays (collective event with two hosts), asserting each host's calendar receives the event and no crash occurs when it is absent.
finding.title: No tests cover the destinationCalendar single-object-to-array conversion
finding.trigger: The PR converts destinationCalendar to an array and touches booking creation, reschedule, and cancel flows across EventManager and multiple calendar services (google, lark, office365), yet the PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added; edge cases like empty array, null, and multi-host arrays are untested.
finding.verifier_reason: Test gap observations are valid but this is a test coverage concern, not a concrete bug with proven trigger and impact. The PR explicitly states no tests added, but absence of tests is not itself a defect in the code.

rejected_findings.reason: Test gap observations are valid but this is a test coverage concern, not a concrete bug with proven trigger and impact. The PR explicitly states no tests added, but absence of tests is not itself a defect in the code.

validated_findings.body: With billing disabled, new organizations are created without a slug (breaking org URLs); with billing enabled, the slug is set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug/payment-gated flow.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Organization creation persists the slug under exactly the opposite billing condition from intended.
validated_findings.impact: With billing disabled, new organizations are created without a slug (breaking org URLs); with billing enabled, the slug is set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug/payment-gated flow.
validated_findings.root_cause: Mechanical conversion from `&&`-spread to ternary-spread accidentally removed the `!` operator.
validated_findings.title: IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition inverted when spreading organization slug
validated_findings.trigger: An organization is created via the create handler in either billing mode: the original code set `slug` only when team billing was NOT enabled (`...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`), but the rewrite dropped the negation.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows L151 changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to R151 `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. The negation was dropped, inverting the condition for when slug is set.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize destinationCalendar to `[]` instead of `null` in the evt construction (or assign `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`).
validated_findings.title: Team hosts' destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has none
validated_findings.trigger: A collective team booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `null` at R1067) but other hosts do have destination calendars.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch R1077-1079 shows `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. When destinationCalendar is null (R1067), optional chaining makes push a no-op, silently discarding team calendars.

validated_findings.body: Downstream code that previously relied on `user.organization.slug` for dynamic bookings (e.g., org-scoped booker URLs/usernames) receives undefined, producing incorrect links or behavior for organization users.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silent loss of a queried field changes the shape of loaded users for dynamic bookings.
validated_findings.impact: Downstream code that previously relied on `user.organization.slug` for dynamic bookings (e.g., org-scoped booker URLs/usernames) receives undefined, producing incorrect links or behavior for organization users.
validated_findings.root_cause: The rewrite of loadUsers omitted the previously selected organization relation from the findMany select clause.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Re-add `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` to the prisma select in the !eventTypeId branch, or verify and document that no consumer reads user.organization after loadUsers.
validated_findings.title: loadUsers refactor drops the organization slug from the dynamic-booking user query
validated_findings.trigger: A dynamic group booking (no eventTypeId) is created for users belonging to an organization; loadUsers now selects only userSelect fields, credentials, and metadata.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Candidate cites LEFT side line 737 showing organization select was removed. However, the patch context shows this is the old code being replaced. The new code structure is different but the claim about downstream usage of organization.slug is speculative without evidence of actual consumers.

validated_findings.body: The same calendar events are deleted N times (once per reference); subsequent attempts hit already-deleted events, generating avoidable API errors/rejections in the awaited Promise.all and log noise.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate delete requests against calendar APIs during recurring cancellation.
validated_findings.impact: The same calendar events are deleted N times (once per reference); subsequent attempts hit already-deleted events, generating avoidable API errors/rejections in the awaited Promise.all and log noise.
validated_findings.root_cause: Wrapping the existing single-reference logic in a loop without excluding the branch that already iterates over all credentials and bookings.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Hoist the recurring-event bulk-deletion branch out of the per-reference loop (run it once), keeping only the single-event `deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` path per reference.
validated_findings.title: Recurring-event deletion block now runs once per calendar reference, issuing duplicate deletes
validated_findings.trigger: Cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring team event whose booking has two or more calendar references with credentialIds: the recurring branch inside the new per-reference loop iterates all user calendar credentials and all updated bookings for every reference.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows a refactor of cancellation logic. The candidate claims duplicate deletes, but the new loop iterates per-reference and the recurring branch is not shown in the provided patch context. Cannot verify the duplicate deletion claim from available evidence.

validated_findings.body: TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`) is thrown at EventManager.create, aborting booking creation entirely for users who select Google Meet without a destination calendar, instead of the intended fallback to Cal Video.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled runtime TypeError during booking creation breaks the Google Meet -> Cal Video fallback path for any host lacking a destination calendar.
validated_findings.impact: TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`) is thrown at EventManager.create, aborting booking creation entirely for users who select Google Meet without a destination calendar, instead of the intended fallback to Cal Video.
validated_findings.root_cause: Changing CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar from a single nullable object to a nullable array introduced array destructuring at consumer sites; the destructured element can be undefined for empty/null arrays, but TypeScript types it as DestinationCalendar, so the missing optional chain in EventManager.create's Meet fallback check was not caught.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the destructured value: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` (or an explicit length/null check) in EventManager.create before accessing `.integration`; alternatively type the destructured element as possibly undefined and handle it.
validated_findings.title: Array conversion of destinationCalendar leaves unguarded dereference crashing Google Meet fallback
validated_findings.trigger: A booking is created with location set to Google Meet (MeetLocationType) while evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (e.g., organizer has no destination calendar configured); EventManager.create destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without a guard.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Same issue as candidate 0: missing optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration causing TypeError. Same root cause, same fix location. Merging into candidate 0.

validated_findings.body: For collective events whose organizer lacks a destination calendar, the other hosts' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are never added to the event, so those hosts do not receive calendar events — defeating the PR's stated purpose of inviting all collective hosts correctly.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silent data loss: valid team host destination calendars are discarded without any error, producing bookings that skip some hosts' calendars.
validated_findings.impact: For collective events whose organizer lacks a destination calendar, the other hosts' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are never added to the event, so those hosts do not receive calendar events — defeating the PR's stated purpose of inviting all collective hosts correctly.
validated_findings.root_cause: The array-typed field allows a null base value, and the aggregation code appends team calendars with optional chaining, silently skipping the append when the base is null instead of creating the array.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize evt.destinationCalendar to an empty array (or `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`) so team destination calendars are always appended regardless of the organizer's configuration.
validated_findings.title: Team hosts' destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
validated_findings.trigger: A COLLECTIVE team booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar: handleNewBooking initializes `destinationCalendar: ... : null`, so the later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` optional-chains into a no-op even when other team hosts do have destination calendars.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Same issue as candidate 8: team calendars dropped when destinationCalendar is null due to optional chaining on push. Same root cause and fix. Merging into candidate 8.

validated_findings.body: The mandatory second parameter is a breaking change to the widely implemented Calendar contract: single-argument call sites fail type-checking, and 12 implementations silently ignore a value the interface now claims is required, misleading future implementers.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Compile-time breakage for external/one-argument callers and a misleading contract where most implementations do not honor the required parameter.
validated_findings.impact: The mandatory second parameter is a breaking change to the widely implemented Calendar contract: single-argument call sites fail type-checking, and 12 implementations silently ignore a value the interface now claims is required, misleading future implementers.
validated_findings.root_cause: The interface was tightened to a required parameter to serve a single implementation's need instead of using an optional parameter.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Declare the parameter as optional (`credentialId?: number`) in the Calendar interface, since CalendarManager always supplies it and only GoogleCalendarService needs it, preserving compatibility for existing single-argument callers.
validated_findings.title: Calendar.createEvent gains a required credentialId parameter used by only one implementation
validated_findings.trigger: Any caller of the shared Calendar interface (tests, API handlers, third-party app-store integrations, or future code) that invokes `calendar.createEvent(event)` with a single argument; among the 13 in-repo CalendarService implementations, only googlecalendar consumes the new parameter.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The interface change to require credentialId is intentional design. CalendarManager.createEvent always passes credential.id (L236). The 12 implementations not using it is existing behavior, not a regression. This is a design/style concern, not a bug.

validated_findings.body: Regressions in the null/empty-array handling paths (e.g., the Meet fallback crash and silent team-calendar drop) can ship undetected, and future refactors of destinationCalendar consumers have no safety net.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Review and CI cannot detect breakage in the many consumer sites rewritten for the array type, leaving the collective multi-host behavior unverified.
validated_findings.impact: Regressions in the null/empty-array handling paths (e.g., the Meet fallback crash and silent team-calendar drop) can ship undetected, and future refactors of destinationCalendar consumers have no safety net.
validated_findings.root_cause: A cross-cutting data-shape change to a core type was merged without any accompanying test coverage of the new array semantics.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add unit/integration tests exercising EventManager.create and handleNewBooking with destinationCalendar as null, empty array, single-element, and multi-host arrays (collective event with two hosts), asserting each host's calendar receives the event and no crash occurs when it is absent.
validated_findings.title: No tests cover the destinationCalendar single-object-to-array conversion
validated_findings.trigger: The PR converts destinationCalendar to an array and touches booking creation, reschedule, and cancel flows across EventManager and multiple calendar services (google, lark, office365), yet the PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added; edge cases like empty array, null, and multi-host arrays are untested.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test gap observations are valid but this is a test coverage concern, not a concrete bug with proven trigger and impact. The PR explicitly states no tests added, but absence of tests is not itself a defect in the code.
